corpus.hash_policy: SHA256 of canonical JSON records sorted by chunk_id, with chunk_id, document_id, text; UTF-8, sorted object keys, compact separators.

reference_policy: Examples of correct synthesis, not exact-match targets. References and evaluation labels must never enter generation prompts.

correctness.rule: 1: substantive factual claims are accurate according to the corpus. 0: a claim contradicts the corpus or cannot be validated from it. Omissions affect completeness. A pure refusal is N/A.

groundedness.rule: 1: every substantive factual claim follows from the actual supplied context. 0: any claim adds unsupported information, even if factually correct.

completeness.rule: For answerable cases, each required point receives 1 only when correctly expressed. Score = satisfied points / total required points. Refusal cases are N/A. Also report evidence-group coverage: a group passes only when all mapped points pass. Keep the full-reference denominator even when retrieval misses evidence.

refusal_correctness.rule: 1: answers supported parts and abstains on unsupported parts, or justifiably refuses an unsupported request. 0: invents missing content or refuses despite sufficient supplied evidence. A refusal followed by unsupported content fails.

citation_correctness.rule: 1: every substantive factual claim has an identifiable supporting citation, and every citation resolves to a supplied source supporting its associated claim. 0: missing, fabricated, mismatched, or non-supporting citations. Pure refusals without factual claims are N/A.

prompt_compliance.rule: Separate check of the current prompt instructions, including exact refusal wording and output structure when applicable. Never include in refusal correctness or an aggregate quality score.

handling_rules: Deterministic means fixed checklists and repeatable human semantic review, not keyword matching or deterministic model output.
Reference answers are synthesis examples, not exact-match targets. Accept equivalent paraphrases and reordered sentences; preserve distinctions, causality, and qualifiers such as may.
Partial correct supported answers can pass correctness and groundedness with fractional completeness. Omissions alone are not factual errors.
Inspect context sufficiency before reviewing the response. A justified refusal on a corpus-answerable case may pass refusal correctness while full-task completeness remains low.
With partial context, accept supported points plus an explicit limitation for missing parts. Full refusal may be justified but earns no factual completeness credit.
A corpus-correct fact absent from supplied context may pass correctness but fails groundedness.
A world-knowledge claim absent from the corpus fails groundedness and corpus-only correctness validation; this does not necessarily mean it is false.
Refusal followed by the unsupported F1 formula or Bankers algorithm fails refusal correctness and groundedness.
Pure refusals need no citation. Optional factual explanations in refusal cases still need supporting citations.
Valid citation syntax alone is insufficient; a source list in the UI alone is insufficient without association to the claim.
Flag unresolved interpretations for manual adjudication before final scoring. Do not guess or consult outside knowledge.
Report dimensions separately with eligible denominators; do not produce a single weighted quality score.

cases.reference_answer: A learning rate that is too large may cause gradient descent to diverge.

required_points.text: An excessively large learning rate may cause divergence.

cases.review_notes: Do not require an additional mechanism or example; preserve may.

cases.reference_answer: Accuracy can be misleading on imbalanced datasets.

required_points.text: Identify imbalanced datasets as the condition.

forbidden_or_unsupported_points: Invented numerical imbalance examples or thresholds.
cases.review_notes: No alternative metric or detailed explanation of the mechanism is required.

cases.reference_answer: Processes have separate memory spaces and usually communicate through inter-process communication mechanisms. Threads within a process share memory, making communication easier.

required_points.text: Processes have separate memory.
Threads within one process share memory.
Process communication usually uses IPC.
Shared memory facilitates thread communication.

cases.review_notes: Accept easier or faster thread communication when supported. Do not require IPC examples or synchronization risks. The explicit IPC point requires os_process_vs_thread chunk 1 or 2; scheduling alternatives support the basic comparison but do not explicitly name IPC.

cases.reference_answer: Aging gradually raises the priority of waiting tasks to reduce starvation.

required_points.text: Gradually increase waiting-task priority.
Connect the priority increase to reducing starvation.

forbidden_or_unsupported_points: A guaranteed waiting-time bound or a specific aging schedule.
cases.review_notes: A definition of starvation alone is incomplete.

required_points.text: Clearly abstain from the requested comparison because supplied notes do not support it.

forbidden_or_unsupported_points: Definitions, mechanisms, or comparisons of dropout and batch normalization.
cases.review_notes: Generic regularization, feature scaling, and database normalization do not support the comparison.

cases.reference_answer: Precision measures the proportion of predicted positive instances that are actually positive.

required_points.text: Identify predicted positives as the population.
Identify actually positive instances within predicted positives.

forbidden_or_unsupported_points: An added mathematical formula absent from the notes.
cases.review_notes: Accept how many predicted positives are actually positive. Reversing the population confuses precision with recall.

cases.reference_answer: This illustrates transitive dependency: department_office depends on department_name rather than student_id. The table is reorganized through decomposition into smaller relations while preserving the meaning of the data.

required_points.text: Identify the specific department dependency as transitive.
Describe decomposition into smaller relations.

forbidden_or_unsupported_points: Claiming the notes specify exact replacement tables, columns, primary keys, or foreign keys.
cases.review_notes: The corpus supports general decomposition, not a concrete redesigned schema.

cases.reference_answer: Partial dependency means a non-key attribute depends on only part of a composite key; second normal form removes it. Transitive dependency means a non-key attribute depends on another non-key attribute; third normal form removes it.

required_points.text: Partial dependency: a non-key attribute depends on only part of a composite key.
Second normal form removes partial dependency.
Transitive dependency: a non-key attribute depends on another non-key attribute.
Third normal form removes transitive dependency.

cases.review_notes: Score the four points separately. Correct normal-form names alone are incomplete.

cases.reference_answer: Durability means that a committed transaction's effects persist even after a crash.

required_points.text: Name durability.
Committed effects persist after a crash.

forbidden_or_unsupported_points: Claims that uncommitted changes necessarily survive a crash.
cases.review_notes: Interpret accepted change as committed, not merely submitted.

cases.reference_answer: This is a non-repeatable read: the same query returns different results within one transaction because another transaction changed the data.

required_points.text: Name non-repeatable read.
Repeated reads differ within a transaction because another transaction modified the data.

cases.review_notes: Treat one database operation as the transaction described by the benchmark. Naming a dirty read or lost update is incorrect.

cases.reference_answer: They use different supervised-learning tasks. Predicting whether a message is junk is classification, which predicts discrete categories. Predicting a property's sale price is regression, which predicts continuous numerical values.

required_points.text: Map junk-message prediction to classification and discrete categories.
Map sale-price prediction to regression and continuous values.

cases.review_notes: Both parts require support; their shared supervised-learning category does not make them the same task.

cases.reference_answer: This suggests overfitting: the model performs well on training examples but poorly on unseen examples.

required_points.text: Name overfitting.
Connect overfitting to strong training performance and poor unseen-data performance.

cases.review_notes: Accept suggests or indicates. Remedies and further causal explanations are optional only when supported.

cases.reference_answer: K-fold cross-validation divides the data into k subsets, with each subset serving as the validation set once across repeated training runs. This reduces the risk of relying on a single train-test split.

required_points.text: Divide data into k subsets.
Rotate validation so each subset is held out once.
Reduce reliance on one train-test split.

forbidden_or_unsupported_points: Guarantees of unbiased estimates or eliminating overfitting.
cases.review_notes: Rotation-only evidence does not support the single-split rationale.

cases.reference_answer: An update anomaly occurs when a repeated fact is changed in some places but other copies are missed. The department example illustrates transitive dependency because department_office depends on department_name rather than student_id.

required_points.text: Explain inconsistent updating of repeated facts.
Identify and explain the department example as transitive dependency.

forbidden_or_unsupported_points: Claiming update anomalies and transitive dependencies are mutually exclusive.
cases.review_notes: Distinguish an inconsistent-update problem from a dependency structure; both can relate to the same table.

cases.reference_answer: Atomicity guarantees that all operations in a transaction happen or none happen. Precision measures the proportion of predicted positive instances that are actually positive.

required_points.text: Transaction operations are all-or-none.
Precision concerns actually positive instances among predicted positives.

cases.review_notes: Require support for both topics. One source covering one topic cannot support the whole answer.

cases.reference_answer: Each thread has its own stack and program counter, even though threads within the process share memory and resources.

required_points.text: Each thread has its own stack.
Each thread has its own program counter.

forbidden_or_unsupported_points: Additional private execution-state items not named in the supplied notes.
cases.review_notes: A bare list of both items is complete; the shared-memory qualification is optional.

cases.reference_answer: First-come first-served is simple but can produce poor average waiting time. Round robin assigns a fixed time quantum and cycles through ready tasks, improving responsiveness.

required_points.text: FCFS can produce poor average waiting time.
Round robin uses a fixed time quantum and cycles through ready tasks.
Round robin improves responsiveness.

forbidden_or_unsupported_points: Claims that round robin always minimizes waiting time or guarantees an optimal quantum.
cases.review_notes: Prefer poor average waiting time; accept long waiting times.

required_points.text: Abstain from giving the requested exact formula.

forbidden_or_unsupported_points: The F1 formula in symbolic, verbal, equivalent, or derived form.
cases.review_notes: The corpus says F1 combines precision and recall but supplies no formula. Any optional description must be cited and retain the refusal.

required_points.text: Abstain from explaining Banker's algorithm or its deadlock handling.

forbidden_or_unsupported_points: Algorithm steps, safety tests, allocation procedures, or deadlock explanations supplied from model memory.
cases.review_notes: General process, scheduling, and starvation notes do not support this request.
